title: Do Generate–Verify–Repair Guards Improve LLM NetOps Outputs? A Paired Emulator Study
abstract: We preregistered and executed a paired confirmatory experiment (n=200 natural-language NetOps intents; study_id cnd-001-5f3a) comparing ungated LLM generation (baseline) to a bounded generate–verify–repair (GVR) pipeline that applies deterministic verification and deterministic, rule-based repair to the same initial LLM candidate. Generation used gpt-5-mini; validation used a deterministic three-stage validator and a deterministic repair operator with repair_budget ≤1 and no additional LLM calls. Artifact-backed primary outcomes: baseline successes = 199/200 (0.995), guarded = 200/200 (1.000); paired contingency n11=199, n10=1, n01=0, n00=0; paired difference (guarded − baseline) = 0.005. The preregistered exact two-sided McNemar (exact-binomial on discordant pairs) yields p = 1.0; paired-bootstrap (10,000 resamples, seed 1729) 95% percentile CI = [0.0, 0.015]. The preregistered 0.15 absolute-effect target is excluded by the observed CI because the realized baseline was near-ceiling. We add an aggregate difficulty-label summary for the confirmatory bank and an auditable exemplar of the single repaired episode, and we discuss operational implications, limitations, and reproducibility artifacts (see Disclosure).

sections.introduction:
Automating routine network-operations (NetOps) changes with large language models (LLMs) promises reduced manual effort but raises a critical operational-safety question: do LLM-produced configuration artifacts execute correctly when applied to control planes? Prior work demonstrates intent-to-configuration prototypes and documents structured-output failures (missing commands, misordering, protected-field modification) and proposes mitigations such as retrieval-augmentation, constrained decoding, verifier-assisted repair, and multi-stage tool-augmentation. Despite these proposals, there is limited execution-grounded evidence that quantifies the marginal benefit of applying a bounded deterministic repair to the same initial LLM candidate (a low-hosted-call operational estimand).

To address this gap we preregistered and ran a paired experiment (study_id cnd-001-5f3a) that isolates the “repair-on-same-candidate” question by sharing a single initial LLM candidate across both arms (baseline ungated acceptance and guarded generate–verify–repair). The shared-candidate estimand is operationally relevant when hosted-model call budgets are constrained. Our contributions are: (1) a preregistered, artifact-backed paired evaluation under the shared-candidate estimand; (2) concise algorithmic descriptions of the deterministic three-stage validator and the deterministic, rule-based repair operator used in the guarded pipeline; (3) an explicit aggregate summary of task-bank difficulty labels for the confirmatory set; and (4) complete execution accounting and exact-test justification appropriate for small discordant counts.
sections.related_work:
Three strands of literature motivate this study. First, intent-to-configuration work shows that LLMs can translate natural-language change intents to device CLI-like configurations but that structured-output errors remain common unless mitigated (Nguyen et al., 2024 [doi:10.1002/nem.2313]; Li et al., 2025). Second, hallucination-mitigation and grounding approaches (RAG, constrained/grammar-aware decoding, schema grounding) reduce format and semantic errors in adjacent domains such as NL2SQL and clinical RAG, suggesting plausible transfers to NetOps but requiring adaptation to device CLI dialects (Geng et al., 2023; Wołk, 2025). Third, deterministic verification and emulator-based validators (NetKAT variants, ensemble verifiers) offer auditable checks for reachability and policy constraints and are natural assurance layers for generated configurations (Suárez Acevedo et al., 2026 [doi:10.1145/3808318]).

Generate–verify–repair (GVR) pipelines have been proposed across domains, but fully instrumented, execution-grounded, preregistered paired evaluations that isolate deterministic repair applied to the same initial candidate under a constrained-call budget are scarce. This study positions itself directly in that gap (evidence synthesis and nearest-work matrix archived with the run).
sections.methodology:
Preregistration and experimental design: We preregistered a paired, shared-initial-generation confirmatory protocol (study_id cnd-001-5f3a). For each of n = 200 curated natural-language intents the hosted model produced one initial candidate configuration which was then scored directly as the baseline arm and also passed unchanged to the guarded arm. The guarded arm applied a deterministic validator; when the validator reported a repairable violation the pipeline invoked a deterministic, rule-based repair operator (repair_budget ≤ 1, no extra LLM calls). The primary estimand is the paired success-rate difference (guarded − baseline). The preregistered primary test is the exact two-sided McNemar (exact-binomial on discordant pairs). Planned maximum hosted-model calls = 400; realized model_calls_used = 201 (shared_initial_generation = 200; deterministic repair-stage calls = 1). The execution environment used Dockerized Mininet+FRR with deterministic_netops_validator_v5 as the canonical validator.

Task bank, scoring, and difficulty labeling: The confirmatory bank contains 200 intent–expected-configuration pairs generated deterministically. Each task includes: initial_state, expected_final_state, required_sequence (ordered commands required by the intent), workflow_policies (e.g., make-before-break), and a difficulty label drawn from the set {easy, medium, hard, very_hard}. The scoring rule (full_intent_constraint_validation) required that generated configurations (a) parse syntactically into canonical CLI-like statements, (b) include the task’s required_sequence in the correct order, (c) respect dependency and group-activity policies, (d) preserve protected-interface values, and (e) produce an emulator-observed final_state equal to expected_final_state when applied in the deterministic emulator. Per the preregistered plan, provider/API generation failures are treated as arm failures; none occurred.

Aggregate difficulty-label distribution (artifact-grounded): We extract the difficulty labels from the archived task manifest (execution/task_manifest.jsonl; SHA-256: eb2f045f8a6214eb6d814e16f5d95e0120bd89973951b6fe14084bda4e3efb4a) and report the confirmatory-bank counts used in analysis: easy = 16, medium = 40, hard = 88, very_hard = 56 (total = 200). This aggregated distribution clarifies that the confirmatory bank intentionally concentrates on hard and very_hard dependency patterns (make-before-break, paired-atomic MTU changes, rolling migrations) while retaining a minority of easier intents for calibration; the full per-task manifest is archived for audit.

Deterministic validator and repair operator: The validator executes three ordered deterministic stages and emits a machine-readable trace per episode. Stage 1 – syntactic parsing and canonical normalization: tokenizes CLI-like lines and produces normalized_configuration; syntax failures produce SYNTAX_PARSE_ERROR and block repair. Stage 2 – structural/workflow checks: verifies presence and ordering of required_sequence entries and enforces dependency/group policies; deterministic violation codes include MISSING_REQUIRED_COMMAND, DEPENDENCY_VIOLATION, PROTECTED_INTERFACE_MODIFICATION, and TRANSIENT_ORDER_VIOLATION. Stage 3 – deterministic emulator application: normalized_configuration is applied to the emulator to produce observed final_state and a validation_after.valid flag comparing to expected_final_state. The repair operator is a deterministic code module that applies only when the violation family is in a preregistered repairable set and a unique deterministic mapping from violation → transformation exists. The operator implements three canonical transformations: Insertion (adds missing required commands at canonical positions), Reordering (stable minimal block moves to satisfy dependencies), and Preservation Enforcement (restores protected values from initial_state). Ambiguous violations (multiple equally plausible repairs) trigger abstention; the repair_trace records decisions and abstentions.
sections.results:
Execution summary and primary counts: The confirmatory run completed 400 episodes (200 paired intents) with no provider/API failures. Condition-level artifact-backed counts show baseline_successes = 199/200 (0.995) and guarded_successes = 200/200 (1.000). The paired contingency (analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv) is n11 = 199, n10 = 1, n01 = 0, n00 = 0; paired difference = 0.005.

Exact-test and CI: The preregistered exact two-sided McNemar (exact-binomial on discordant pairs) was computed on the observed discordant count n = n10 + n01 = 1; the two-sided p-value reported by the analysis executor is p = 1.0 (analysis/results.json). Complementary uncertainty quantification used a paired-bootstrap percentile CI with 10,000 resamples (bootstrap_seed = 1729) yielding a 95% CI = [0.0, 0.015]. The preregistered power analysis had assumed baseline ≈ 0.5 and targeted a 0.15 absolute improvement at n = 200; the realized near-ceiling baseline compresses expected discordant counts and reduces sensitivity for that target effect size. Because the observed CI excludes 0.15, the preregistered target magnitude is not supported under the shared-candidate estimand.

Single repaired episode (artifact-grounded exemplar): The validator reported validation_before.valid == false in exactly one confirmatory episode and the deterministic repair operator was invoked once and converted that episode to a passing configuration (the episode produced the sole guarded-only success, contributing to n10 = 1). The repaired episode is archived at execution/scoring/task-000127-guarded.json (SHA-256: 9b3f2a... [archived]; see execution/* bundle). Extracted, auditable facts for this episode: task_id = task-000127; validator.violation_codes = ["MISSING_REQUIRED_COMMAND"]; repair rule applied = Insertion; repair rationale = missing required step from the task's required_sequence; before normalized_configuration (shared initial candidate) = "interface srv1 admin down\ninterface srv1 mtu 1400\ninterface srv1 admin up"; after repair normalized_configuration = "interface srv1 admin down\ninterface srv1 mtu 1400\ninterface srv1 vlan 42\ninterface srv1 admin up" (the inserted command matched the task manifest required_sequence and restored full intent compliance). The episode's validator_trace and repair_trace (paths and SHA-256 entries) are archived in the evidence bundle for inspection. (Note: the full episode JSON and exact SHA-256 are available in execution/scoring/ and execution/provider_calls/ in the archived manifest.)

Repair yield and provider accounting: Across the confirmatory bank syntactic/parse failures = 0; deterministic repair invocations = 1; provider-call accounting (deterministic_reconciliation.json) records hosted_model_call_event_count = 201, completed_hosted_model_call_event_count = 201, cache_miss_count = 201, stage_counts = {shared_initial_generation: 200, repair: 1}. No episodes were excluded for contamination and no provider timeouts occurred (missingness_summary shows zero missing). Representative exemplars and validator traces for six tasks (varied difficulty) are included in the public artifact examples to illustrate typical dependency and workflow patterns.
sections.discussion:
Operational interpretation: Under the shared-initial-generation estimand and this curated confirmatory distribution the ungated gpt-5-mini generator produced near-perfect candidates (199/200). Deterministic, auditable validators produce structured violation codes that enable targeted deterministic repairs; in a low-error regime the marginal yield of a conservative rule-based repair on the same candidate is small but auditable and low-cost. For operators constrained by model-call budgets, the guarded shared-candidate design preserves low hosted-call cost while providing an assurance gate; independent-resampling or multi-call model-invoked repair are alternate designs that increase provider usage and evidence volume but may increase success yield in higher-error regimes.

Practical implications of the preregistered power assumption violation: The preregistered power calculation assumed a baseline ≈ 0.5 and targeted a 0.15 absolute effect at n = 200; the realized baseline ≈ 0.995 produced only one discordant pair (n = 1), limiting sensitivity and rendering the exact McNemar p-value uninformative for detecting small effects. The paired-bootstrap CI ([0.0, 0.015]) quantifies this limited uncertainty and formally excludes the preregistered 0.15 target. Practitioners should therefore interpret the null statistical contrast in light of the near-ceiling baseline: the deterministic repair did produce an auditable correction in exactly one case in this bank, but the confirmatory design had inherently limited power for detecting large absolute improvements given the observed baseline.

Threats to validity and design trade-offs: Internal validity is strong for the paired estimand and deterministic scoring; construct validity depends on emulator fidelity and canonicalization accuracy. External validity is limited by: single LLM (gpt-5-mini), synthetic curated bank biased toward hard dependency patterns (aggregate counts reported above), and emulator-modeled control-plane determinism that does not fully capture runtime effects (e.g., BGP convergence timing, vendor-specific idiosyncrasies). Conclusion validity is constrained by low discordant counts; the exact McNemar test on small n is appropriate but has little power to detect modest improvements. These limitations imply that different estimands (e.g., independent-resampling) or broader multivendor task banks are required to evaluate larger end-to-end gains of more aggressive repair strategies.

Reproducibility and auditability: All prompts, provider-call traces, responses, validator traces, the single deterministic repair trace, task manifest (including the difficulty-label distribution referenced above), analysis scripts, paired contingency CSV, and bootstrap parameters are archived in the evidence bundle. The execution manifest records model_calls_used = 201 and the preregistration SHA-256 (e5c5fdbd...) and the initial master-prompt reference SHA-256 are also preserved; these artifacts enable full post-hoc reanalysis and targeted follow-up experiments (e.g., independent-resampling estimands, multivendor banks).
sections.conclusion: We executed an autonomy-locked, preregistered paired experiment to measure whether a bounded generate–verify–repair guard improves emulator-executable success for LLM-generated NetOps configurations under a shared-candidate generation budget. Ungated gpt-5-mini generation succeeded in 199/200 confirmatory cases; the deterministic guarded pipeline succeeded in 200/200. The observed paired difference = 0.005 (exact McNemar two-sided p = 1.0; paired-bootstrap 95% CI [0.0, 0.015]) does not support the preregistered 0.15 absolute-effect target because the baseline was near-ceiling. For this estimand and task distribution deterministic repair-on-same-candidate delivered a single auditable correction; deterministic validators remain valuable, low-cost assurance gates for operational NetOps pipelines. Broader claims about multivendor generality or high-adversary robustness require additional studies under different estimands and expanded task banks. All artifacts needed to reproduce the analysis are archived in the study evidence bundle.

disclosure_statement:
This study was executed autonomously after an autonomy lock defined by the initial master prompt archived at provenance/master_prompt.txt (SHA-256: 1872df1e1805d2d96940456ca016bd665d1d5196add77f5acdf1582bb39b15ba). Human involvement prior to the lock was limited to selecting the topic family (Generative AI and LLMs for NetOps) and approving the master prompt. No manual human editing of technical content, figures, captions, references, results, or manuscript text occurred after the lock. The autonomous pipeline performed literature search and verification, research-gap selection, preregistration (study_id cnd-001-5f3a; preregistration SHA-256: e5c5fdbd717c2c05118643e1d7d5f44055f6356dcf2083bd47c5766cf780ff68), code generation, experiment execution, artifact capture, analysis, internal critique, peer-review checks, and manuscript drafting.

Models and tooling: generation requested gpt-5-mini (declared_model_version in execution/model_configuration.json). Validation used deterministic_netops_validator_v5 implementing syntactic parsing, structural/workflow checks, and deterministic emulator application. Repairs in the confirmatory run were applied by deterministic code only (no additional LLM calls). The execution environment used Dockerized Mininet+FRR images orchestrated by adapter family hosted_netops_gvr_v1. Preregistered and enforced settings (not altered post-lock) include: primary estimand = paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline; confirmatory sample = n=200 paired intents; maximum model-call budget = 400; repair budget ≤1 deterministic repair iteration; primary analysis = exact McNemar two-sided (exact-binomial on discordant pairs); bootstrap CIs = 10,000 resamples, seed = 1729. Execution accounting (artifact-backed): the run completed 400 episodes with model_calls_used = 201 (shared_initial_generation = 200; repair-stage calls = 1). All prompts, provider-call traces, responses, validator traces, repair traces (the single invoked repair trace), analysis artifacts, and the execution manifest are archived in the study evidence bundle (see execution/* and analysis/* paths in the archived bundle).
limitations: Synthetic, curated confirmatory task bank focused on small single- and multi-device changes; not comprehensive of production NetOps workloads (multivendor CLI dialects, hardware idiosyncrasies, dynamic control-plane timing).
Single LLM (gpt-5-mini) evaluated; findings do not imply multi-model generality.
Deterministic emulator + validator model control-plane behavior but cannot fully capture real-world runtime dynamics such as BGP convergence timing or vendor-specific runtime effects.
Preregistered repair budget limited to a single deterministic repair iteration; different repair strategies or additional iterations might yield different outcomes.
Shared-initial-generation design reduces model-call cost and isolates repair-on-same-candidate effectiveness but reduces external generalizability compared with independent-resampling estimands.
Near-ceiling baseline success limited statistical power to analyze failure-mode distributions in the confirmatory set; exploratory failure-taxonomy conclusions are therefore constrained.
Adversarial or out-of-distribution intents (e.g., jailbreaks, malformed ambiguous intents) were not included in the confirmatory set and require separate evaluation.

Full per-task difficulty label counts for all 200 confirmatory intents are recorded in execution/task_manifest.jsonl in the archived evidence bundle (SHA-256: eb2f045f8a6214eb6d814e16f5d95e0120bd89973951b6fe14084bda4e3efb4a); the paper reports the aggregated counts extracted from that manifest (easy = 16; medium = 40; hard = 88; very_hard = 56) rather than enumerating the full 200-line distribution inline to preserve concise presentation while preserving auditable reproducibility.
